correctness.rationale: The exact domain Q, Neumann-generator normalization, TV convention and corner starts are specified. A killed-two-particle determinant establishes strict TP2; reflection yields the exact triangle sign region, giving an attained optimal measurable test. Explicit integrated cosine modes produce the displayed absolutely convergent double series; first nonzero exponents 1,5,9 give the long-time asymptotic. The Gaussian-unfolding coupling (error O(sqrt(t) exp(-1/(4t)))) and a rotated independent-Gaussian tail yield the short-time coefficient. Standalone quadrature/spectral checks agree to <7e-8 for times tested; finite numerics are not used as proofs.

originality.rationale: The new claim is an exact *specified opposite-corner* two-dimensional total-variation profile, including the diagonal likelihood crossing, a genuine mixed k^2+l^2 spectral correction with exponent 5, and the geometric short-time exponent 1/8. Loper 2018 gives a diameter-based upper bound (and a sharp one-dimensional benchmark), not this two-dimensional equality; Karlin-McGregor and Kolokoltsov supply total-positivity/monotonicity ingredients but not the product-kernel triangular integration. Actual published-finding corpus and all accessible own 103 previous claims were checked. Residual risk of an unindexed explicit square calculation remains.

value.rationale: The chosen invariant is a natural binary discrimination/mixing benchmark between the furthest two starting corners of the first nontrivial reflected product diffusion. Prior convex-domain bounds control it only by a non-sharp diameter envelope. Determining the exact optimal decision set, the first mixed spectral frequency 5 (versus 9 for the one-dimensional odd series), and the sharp short-time geometric barrier 1/8 gives an interpretable, reproducible dimension-two benchmark; the fact is not a gratuitous fixed table entry. The result is intentionally not inflated to a globally optimized semigroup coefficient.
